headline: Zoo Staff Scale Cliffs to Save Rarest Snails on Earth
meta_description: Chester Zoo conservationists bred and released 300 Madeiran land snails back to their remote island home, saving the species from extinction.
summary_short: In a dramatic cliff rescue, zoo experts returned 300 tiny snails to Portugal's Bugio Island, where only 21 of the species remained in the wild.
body:
In a race against extinction, conservationists from Chester Zoo have bred 300 Madeiran land snails and successfully reintroduced them to the remote Portuguese island where the species clings to survival. Just 21 of these thumbnail-sized creatures were found clinging to a single rock on Bugio Island in the Madeira archipelago when experts arrived. The reintroduction required scaling treacherous cliffs under dangerous conditions—the team had to jump from the water, climb the rock face in darkness, and navigate cracks where the snails could be safely left. With only a narrow window before rough weather forced their departure and no jetty to dock safely, every moment counted. As Tamas Papp, assistant team manager for invertebrates at Chester Zoo, explained: the stakes could not have been higher.

These snails, measuring barely 8mm across, play an outsized role in their ecosystem by eating vegetation and enriching the soil. Though tiny, they represent the last hope for an entire species—a responsibility that shaped every decision during the perilous rescue. The Madeira government had specifically requested Chester Zoo's expertise for this conservation mission, recognizing that without intervention, the snails faced certain extinction.

Now the real work of restoration begins. The newly released snails will be carefully monitored as they settle back into their natural habitat, with conservationists hoping that this bold reintroduction marks not an ending, but a new chapter for a species that nearly vanished forever.
quick_facts: 300 Madeiran land snails bred and released on Bugio Island
Only 21 snails remained in the wild before reintroduction
Each snail measures 8mm—smaller than a third of an inch
Chester Zoo team scaled cliffs in darkness without a dock
Snails enrich soil and control vegetation in their ecosystem
